title: Dalmelitinib Plus Aumolertinib in Advanced NSCLC Patients With EGFR-TKI Resistance and <i>MET</i> Amplification: A Randomized Phase 3 Trial.
journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
abstract: MET amplification accounts for up to 30% of acquired resistance to EGFR-TKI, especially following third-generation EGFR-TKI treatment, yet precision-targeted therapeutic options remain limited.
Early-phase studies demonstrated promising antitumor activity with the MET-TKI dalmelitinib combined with the third-generation EGFR-TKI aumolertinib.
This phase 3 trial compared dalmelitinib-aumolertinib with platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR -mutated, MET -amplified advanced NSCLC after EGFR-TKIs progression.
This randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial (NCT06110663) enrolled patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR -mutated, MET -amplified NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression.
MET amplification was defined by fluorescence in situ hybridization as a mean MET copy number ≥5 or MET / CEP7 ratio ≥2.
Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib or platinum-based chemotherapy groups.
The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1.
Secondary endpoints included overall survival, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), and safety.
A total of 314 enrolled patients were assigned to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib (n=156) or platinum-based chemotherapy (n=158).
Median follow-up was 11.2 months at the data cutoff date (December 10, 2025).
Median PFS was 6.2 months with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and 4.4 months with chemotherapy (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.81; P EGFR -mutated, MET -amplified NSCLC after progression on EGFR-TKI.
These findings support dual EGFR/ MET inhibition as a new treatment option in this biomarker selected population.
